text.p: Lenny Webster's single in the
bottom of the 10th inning scored Rafael Palmeiro with the
winning run as the Baltimore Orioles kept rolling with a 5-4
come-from-behind victory over the Anaheim Angels Sunday.
Palmeiro started the 10th by walking against reliever
Shigetoshi Hasegawa (2-6) and moved up on a balk. After Cal
Ripken popped out trying to bunt and Brady Anderson was
intentionally walked, Webster worked the count to 3-2 before
singling inside the left-field line.
"It doesn't surprise me that any one of the 25 players on
this roster becomes a hero because we have a good group of
players, good role-players that come in and contribute," said
Webster, who had two hits and is 8-for-20 in August.
The Orioles won in their final at-bat for the 10th time
this year and posted their 32nd come-from-behind win. They
have won 15 of their last 20 games and have a 4 1/2-game lead
over the second-place Yankees in the American League East.
Five of Baltimore's last seven wins have been by one run.
"It always seems to be a struggle," manager Davey Johnson
said. "It seems like all we do is play one-run games or
extra-inning games lately."
Armando Benitez (3-3) pitched a hitless 10th for the win.
Ripken had a leadoff double in the second for his 922nd
extra-base hit, moving past Goose Goslin into 33rd place
all-time.
In New York, Ramiro Mendoza threw six scoreless innings in
relief of an injured David Cone and Tim Raines and Paul
O'Neill each drove in three runs to lead the Yankees to an 8-0
rout of the Texas Rangers.
Cone pitched just one inning before he was forced to leave
due to tightness in his right shoulder. He was to be
re-examined on Monday.
Mendoza (5-5), who allowed three runs in the 10th inning
and was the losing pitcher in Saturday's game against the
Rangers, allowed just two hits in his longest outing of the
season. He walked one and struck out three.
The Yankees have won 15 of their last 20.
In Cleveland, Roger Clemens struck out 11 in seven innings
to earn his major league-best 19th win and Jose Cruz Jr hit a
three-run homer in a seven-run fourth inning as the Toronto
Blue Jays rolled over the Indians, 10-5.
Clemens (19-4) struck out the side in the first inning but
gave up a three-run double to Sandy Alomar in the second to
trail 3-0. Then he settled down to yield just one run, three
hits and two walks over the next five innings. Clemens was
charged with four runs, six hits and three walks.
Clemens, whose 1.78 ERA is best in the American League,
last had 19 wins in 1987 when he finished 20-9 and won the Cy
Young Award. He fanned 10 or more for the 11th time this year.
His 226 strikeouts are second to Seattle's Randy Johnson.
Clemens, 10-1 in 12 starts on the road this season, won
for the first time in five starts at Jacobs Field (1-2). That
had been the only A.L. ballpark where he had not won.
In Chicago, the Mariners and White Sox split a twin bill.
Jeff Fassero (12-7) allowed one run over seven innings and
Ken Griffey Jr hit a pair of home runs to become the first
player to reach 40 this year as Seattle won 5-3.
Griffey hit a two-run homer in the first and a solo shot
in the ninth for his fourth 40-homer season in five years.
Jay Buhner added a solo homer for the Mariners, his 30th,
and became the first player in team history to hit 30 homers
in three straight seasons.
But the White Sox took the nightcap when Mike Sirotka
combined with four relievers on an eight-hitter for his first
win of the season and Ozzie Guillen had two hits and an RBI in
a 4-2 victory.
Sirotka (1-0), who spent most of the season in the minors,
allowed one run and five hits in 5 1/3 innings with a walk and
five strikeouts. He escaped jams in the first two innings.
In Milwaukee, after a 3-hour, 49-minute rain delay before
the game, rookie Steve Woodard allowed two runs over five
innings as the Brewers earned a 5-2 victory over the Oakland
Athletics and a sweep of the two-game series.
Woodard (3-1) scattered seven hits, walking none and
striking out five in his fifth major-league start.
Mark Davis, Bob Wickman and Doug Jones, who retired the
side in order in the ninth for his 25th save in 26 chances,
held the Athletics hitless over the final four innings.
Jose Valentin hit a solo homer as five different Brewers
drove in runs.
In Boston, Aaron Sele (12-9) allowed two runs and four
hits in seven innings and eight different players drove in a
run as the Red Sox won their fourth straight, 10-5 over the
Minnesota Twins, who lost their ninth in a row.
In Detroit, Greg Keagle (1-2) allowed three runs over
seven innings for his first win as a starter in the majors and
Travis Fryman had a season-high four RBI to lead the Tigers to
an 8-4 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
